title: Quantum Gravity Simulation: Quantum simulation with a minimum length based on the generalised uncertainty principle
authors: Jack Keable-Elliott, David J. Bacon, Andrew Burbanks, Jaewoo Joo
abstract: We present a recipe for simulating one-dimensional quantum systems for low and high energies with $L$ qubits within the framework of first quantisation. Assuming a minimum grid spacing $ΔL$ in the finite-difference method, the generalised uncertainty principle (GUP) is derived analytically and shows distinct properties for low- and high-energy quantum systems. In the low-energy regime, the GUP approaches to the standard Heisenberg uncertainty principle (HUP) for $ ΔL \ll \hbar$. However, for finite $ΔL \neq 0$, the GUP mathematically provides three different regions dependent on the average momentum and suggests that a wavefunction can exhibit a single-point localisation at the finite momentum uncertainty due to lack of grid resolution. We then derive a new expression for the high-energy momentum and focus on two specific cases relevant to relativistic aspects. First, if the HUP is relaxed and the high-energy momentum is matched to the special-relativistic one, the resulting GUP predicts the existence of a minimum length with non-zero mass for high energy despite the continuous limit $ΔL = 0$. Second, enforcing consistency with the HUP allows the recovery of a canonical high-energy representation with no minimum length. But this requirement brings incompatibility with the special-relativistic momentum and suggests a modified energy-momentum equation. Therefore, we believe that the proposed momentum formulation provides a novel pathway to investigate quantum gravity phenomena for high energy using quantum simulation tools.
summary: This paper proposes a simulation recipe using qubits to study how minimum length scales, derived from the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP), affect quantum systems. By analyzing low- and high-energy limits on a discretized grid, the authors reveal unique dependencies on the lattice spacing ($\Delta L$). The work offers a computational tool to test theoretical predictions about quantum gravity effects.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to simulate quantum gravity phenomena by analyzing the Generalized Uncertainty Principle (GUP) in both low- and high-energy regimes.
main_result: It establishes that incorporating finite grid spacing ($\Delta L$) leads to distinct GUP behaviors, suggesting novel pathways to investigate minimum length effects at high energies, though conflicts arise when enforcing consistency with special relativity versus preserving the standard HUP.
method: The authors use a first-quantization approach on a discretized spatial grid ($L$ qubits) to derive discrete position and momentum operators, allowing for systematic calculation of expectation values under GUP corrections.
model_or_system: The model analyzes one-dimensional quantum systems using localized ansatz states (Gaussian/sinc) simulated via qubit representations. The core physics revolves around modifying the standard uncertainty relation due to hypothesized minimum length scales from quantum gravity.
key_observables: Position uncertainty ($\delta x$), momentum uncertainty ($\delta p_x$ and $\delta p_x^H$), and the resulting GUP inequality $(\delta x)(\delta p) \geq \dots$.
important_parameters: Minimum grid spacing ($\Delta L$), low/high energy regimes, mass ($m$), and fundamental constants ($\hbar$, $c$).
main_assumptions:
The analysis assumes a finite $\Delta L 
eq 0$ for simulation purposes; approximations are made using Taylor expansions when deriving the high-energy momentum operator ($\hat{p}_{H x}$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares low-energy GUP curves from simulation data (Gaussian/sinc states) against theoretical lines. Figure 2 shows mass-dependent high-energy GUP properties for an electron using varying qubit numbers.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the low-energy GUP effects due to discretization ($\Delta L$), then developing a procedure for high-energy momentum operators ($\hat{p}_{H x}$), and finally analyzing the resulting high-energy GUP, highlighting conflicts between relativistic consistency and HUP preservation.
why_interesting: The systematic incorporation of finite lattice spacing into fundamental quantum relations like the uncertainty principle provides a concrete, computational method to explore regimes inaccessible by standard continuum theory in quantum gravity.
